title: Trapping Rain Water
summary: Given an elevation map of bars, compute how much rain water is trapped between them.

tests.explain: Water sits above indices 2 (1 unit), 4 (1), 5 (2), 6 (1) and 9 (1): 6 units in total.
A single bar can't hold water.

hints: Think about one index at a time. How high can water stand above index i?
Water above i is min(highest bar on its left, highest bar on its right) - height[i]. Precomputing both maxima is O(n) time and O(n) space.
To use O(1) space, keep leftMax and rightMax while two pointers walk inward. Whichever side has the smaller max is settled: that max is the bottleneck.

complexity.time: O(n): one pass with two pointers
